query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the in‐flight particle velocity during HVAF-i7 spraying by optimizing the torch parameters (e.g., fuel/oxygen ratios and setting the spray distance near 300–350 mm) will overcome the thickness limitation for FeCoNiCrAl bond coats.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock in the 15–45 μm size range, as used in previous HVAF-M3 depositions.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 process to operate at a higher particle velocity by fine-tuning torch parameters—specifically, adopting a nozzle-to-substrate distance of about 300–350 mm and modifying fuel/oxygen flow to increase particle momentum.
generation.conditions: Deposition on substrates (including those with internal diameters as small as 120 mm) under standard HVAF conditions (typical temperature and atmospheric composition) without changing the powder composition or size distribution.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle kinetic energy resulting in more effective splat formation and inter-particle bonding at impact, thereby increasing deposition efficiency.
generation.mechanism: Higher velocity particles have greater momentum upon impact, which improves flattening and adhesion, leading to a thicker, dense coating. Shorter in-flight residence can also help minimize oxidation by reducing exposure time to oxygen.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increased coating thickness comparable to or exceeding that obtained with the HVAF-M3 torch while retaining excellent adhesion and minimal as-sprayed oxidation; the bond coat will be durable under high-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions.
generation.baseline: HVAF-M3 coatings using 15–45 μm feedstock, and HVAF-i7 coatings produced under current settings that yield acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective for FeCoNiCrAl coatings deposited with HVAF-i7 on substrates with internal diameters down to 120 mm and under standard operating conditions without additional changes to feedstock properties.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvement in thickness is uncertain and may depend on the exact tuning of fuel/oxygen ratios and spray distance. There is also some uncertainty in directly translating deposition improvements from MCrAlY conventional coatings to FeCoNiCrAl HEA systems.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a set of controlled HVAF-i7 depositions on identical substrates using the same FeCoNiCrAl 15–45 μm powder. Compare standard HVAF-i7 parameters with an intervention group where operating parameters are tuned to increase particle velocity (achieving a nozzle distance of 300–350 mm and adjusted fuel/oxygen flows).
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the increased particle velocity fails to produce a statistically significant (and repeatable) increase in bond-coat thickness without degrading adhesion or increasing oxidation relative to the baseline HVAF-i7 deposition, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: As reported in [,,,], HVOF as-sprayed AlTiCrFeCoNi coatings possessed a dense microstructure and a high microhardness over 750 HV with a good fracture toughness. The heat-treated NiCoFeCrSiAlTi coating exhibits a hardness even higher than 800 HV, good wear resistance, and oxidation resistance at 1100 °C, similar to that of MCrAlY coating []. The cavitation erosion resistance of the AlCoCrFeNi coating is about 3.5 times that of 06Cr13Ni5Mo steel in the same environment []. The high wear resistance of AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA at elevated temperatures is associated with oxidation behavior. The formation of a compact oxide layer on the AlCoCrFeNi and AlTiCrFeCoNi HVOF coatings accounts for enhanced wear resistance at temperatures ≥ 800 °C [] and a lowered coefficient of friction due to its function as a solid lubricant []. In [], it was found that additions of Nd and Mo to a AlCrFeCoNi base significantly reduced the wear depth at increasing temperatures due to improved oxide layer adhesion. Thus, AlCoCrFeNiMo coatings deposited using HVOF are suitable for high-temperature application.
